0.0.n: 禍 means calamity; this compound refers to the pandemic and its disruption.

0.1.n: Links the pandemic to the teaching staff, describing their circumstances.

0.2.n: Includes both teachers and other school employees.

0.4.n: Refers to work beyond regular working hours.

0.5.n: Marks overtime as what shows an increasing trend.

0.6.n: Combines with 傾向 to describe an upward trend.

0.7.n: Describes a general direction rather than an increase in every case.

0.8.n: The headline ends here, leaving the final verb unstated.

0.10.n: 文科省 is the abbreviated name of 文部科学省, officially called MEXT in English.

0.11.n: Follows the ministry’s name to identify the source of the findings.

1.0.n: Sets the circumstances in which the working conditions were surveyed.

1.1.n: A formal expression linking a time, place, or situation to the noun phrase that follows.

1.2.n: Refers collectively to teaching and other school personnel.

1.3.n: Links school staff to their working conditions.

1.4.n: Combines with 実態 to refer to actual employment conditions.

1.5.n: Emphasizes what work is really like, rather than official expectations.

1.6.n: The preceding nouns specify whose working conditions were investigated.

1.7.n: Marks the survey as the context in which these findings emerged.

1.9.n: Combines with 期間 to name the time when schools were closed.

1.10.n: Follows 休校 to specify the duration of school closures.

1.11.n: Highlights the closure period, contrasting it with the period after reopening.

1.12.n: Refers to extra work beyond scheduled hours.

1.13.n: Marks overtime as the thing that decreased.

1.14.n: Plain past form of 減る, describing a reduction without naming anyone who caused it.

1.15.n: Follows a complete clause to introduce a contrasting finding.

2.0.n: 後 is attached to 再開 to indicate the time following schools’ reopening.

2.2.n: Shortens 小学校 and 中学校 into one combined expression.

2.3.n: Marks schools as the setting where the overtime trend occurs.

2.4.n: Added after で to make these schools the topic.

2.5.n: Names the school break whose duration was reduced.

2.6.n: Links summer vacation to its shortening.

2.7.n: A noun describing a reduction in the length of the summer break.

2.8.n: Lists examples without suggesting these are the only causes.

2.9.n: Modifies 作業 to specify the kind of work involved.

2.10.n: Refers to practical tasks, here disinfecting school facilities.

2.11.n: Shows that the listed causes are examples, not a complete list.

2.12.n: Marks the preceding activities and changes as causes of increased overtime.

2.13.n: 年度 refers to an institutional year rather than a January-to-December calendar year.

2.14.n: Marks last fiscal year as the baseline for comparison.

2.15.n: Refers to hours worked beyond the regular schedule.

2.16.n: Marks overtime as what is showing an upward trend.

2.17.n: Pairs with 傾向 to describe the direction of change.

2.18.n: Indicates a general tendency rather than a universal or fixed outcome.

2.19.n: With ある, marks the state described by 増加傾向.

2.20.n: In 傾向にある, describes being in a particular trend or tendency.

2.21.n: Turns the preceding statement into a noun-like unit that can be the subject of 分かりました.

2.22.n: Marks the entire finding introduced by こと as what became clear.

2.23.n: Polite past form of 分かる, used in news reports to present findings.

0.lit: Pandemic-era teachers and school staff: overtime toward an increasing trend. Education ministry survey.
0.tip: News headlines often omit final verbs and leave sources as short noun phrases.

1.lit: In a survey of pandemic-era school staff’s actual working conditions, during school closures overtime decreased, whereas...
1.tip: 一方 after a clause signals a contrast, which continues in the next line.

2.lit: After reopening, elementary/junior-high schools’ overtime trended upward versus last fiscal year because of summer-break shortening, disinfection, etc., it became clear.
2.tip: ことが分かりました presents the whole preceding statement as something the survey revealed.
